properties.name: Nothing reflow2 serves names a real person, and a gate keeps it that way
properties.rationale: THE QUESTION WAS A PRIVACY QUESTION AND THE ANSWER WAS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE. Anthony asked whether he was in other people's reflow2 projects by default. Nothing ships him: the kit tarball contains the string zero times, the server never creates a Contributor by itself, never derives one from the environment, the git config or the OS user, and claim_region explicitly refuses an unknown contributor rather than minting one. What the shipped binary did carry was his real id as the ONLY worked example on add_contributor's id parameter, which is the text an agent reads at the exact moment it invents a contributor id. An example is not documentation when the reader is a model; it is a template. THE CLASS WAS VISIBLE IN THE SOURCE AND HAD ALREADY BEEN SOLVED ONCE, TWELVE LINES AWAY. reflow2_init.py's Copilot entry records that product's own help output and an end-to-end confirmation. The examples in the served surface were drawn from whatever real project was at hand instead, and one of them was a different customer's: art:ifc-shell-model and ifc_quantify are bhome's artifact and an IfcMCP tool, shipped to everybody. reflow2 is a wrench for other people's projects and its worked examples were coming from the hands that made it. WHAT THE GATE CAN AND CANNOT SEE, stated because the limit is real: it knows the people THIS design records, which is the population that can leak from here, and it cannot know that art:ifc-shell-model belongs to somebody else because bhome's design is not in this graph. A placeholder convention covers that case and is stated in AGENTS.md rather than checked. ATTRIBUTION IS NOT LOST, IT IS RELOCATED. Who filed a field report belongs in the graph, where it is private to this project and travels with the design; the served text keeps the fact and the date. That is the three-place rule applied to a surface nobody had applied it to.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Every real identifier is out of the served surface. add_contributor's `id` example becomes the house convention `who:<slug>` with an agent id beside it; `handle` offers `@<handle>`; Constraint.limit_source and Snapshot.target_id lose who:ajs; and another project's identifiers, art:ifc-shell-model and ifc_quantify, come out of limit_source by hand. tools/the_served_surface_names_no_real_person.py is a new CI gate reading this design's own Contributors of kind `person` and failing if any id, handle or display name appears in a served tool schema, a schema file describe_schema reads, or a skill body get_skill returns. Observed to FAIL first with nine hits, six of which the hand search had missed: a second user's first name was shipped in schema/structure.yaml, schema/verify.yaml and two skill bodies. Those attributions are now de-identified in the skill SOURCE under getting-started/skills, with both mirrors re-synced. The rank ratchet was re-run because a served description changed, and holds.
